## Summary

`moonbitlang/async/http` can abort while decoding a gzip-compressed HTTP response on native Linux:

```text
panic: load of misaligned address ... for type 'const uint32_t' (aka 'const unsigned int'), which requires 4 byte alignment
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/internal/gzip_internal/metadata.mbt:58:11
```

The same request succeeds if `Accept-Encoding` is forced to `identity`, so the failure appears to be in the gzip response decoding path.

## Minimal repro

`moon.mod`:

```moonbit
name = "repro/async_gzip_repro"

version = "0.1.0"

import {
    "moonbitlang/async@0.20.0",
}

preferred_target = "native"
```

`moon.pkg`:

```moonbit
import {
  "moonbitlang/async",
  "moonbitlang/async/http",
}

supported_targets = "native"

options(
  "is-main": true,
)
```

`main.mbt`:

```moonbit
async fn main {
  let url = "https://mooncakes.io/git/index/info/refs"
  let (resp, body) = @http.get(url, headers={ "User-Agent": "moon" })
  println("status=\{resp.code} bytes=\{body.binary().length()}")
}
```

Run:

```bash
moon -C /tmp/async-gzip-repro run --target native
```

## Actual result

The program aborts while reading the response body:

```text
thread ... panic: load of misaligned address 0x... for type 'const uint32_t' (aka 'const unsigned int'), which requires 4 byte alignment
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/internal/gzip_internal/metadata.mbt:58:11
    is [
          ^
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/internal/gzip_internal/decoder.mbt:383:5
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/http/parser.mbt:106:11
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/http/parser.mbt:66:7
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/http/parser.mbt:176:13
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/http/client.mbt:174:5
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/io/reader.mbt:53:12
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/io/reader.mbt:151:11
_build/_deps/registry-extract/moonbitlang/async/0.20.0/src/http/request.mbt
```

The failing source line is the gzip header pattern in `src/internal/gzip_internal/metadata.mbt`:

```moonbit
guard buf
  is [
    b'\x1f',
    b'\x8b',
    compression_method,
    flags,
    u32le(mtime),
    extra_flags,
    operating_system,
  ] else {
  raise InvalidHeader("invalid gzip magic")
}
```

## Possible root cause / fix layer

This may not be specific to the HTTP gzip implementation itself. The immediate
trigger is `u32le(mtime)` over a `BytesView` slice:

```moonbit
u32le(mtime)
```

`BytesView` can start at any byte offset, so callers generally cannot assume the
underlying address is 4-byte aligned. If this pattern is lowered to a direct
`uint32_t*` load in the native C backend, it can be UB / sanitizer-trapping even
on hardware that otherwise tolerates unaligned accesses.

So one possible local fix is for async gzip metadata parsing to read the gzip
header/trailer integer fields byte-by-byte. But the more general fix might belong
in `moonbitlang/core` or codegen: `u32le` / similar endian patterns over
`BytesView` should probably be unaligned-safe, or the alignment precondition
should be explicit.

title: `@io.pipe()` loses data when a blocked read is cancelled after the writer has already delivered it (deadlock)
Track native async runtime correctness followups found during wasm host port
body:
## Summary

While aligning the wasm host implementation with the native async runtime, a few native-runtime behaviors looked like upstream correctness or portability followups. Tracking them here so the wasm host can keep mirroring native behavior instead of fixing these only in the wasm port.

## Followups

### Windows open ignores `sync`

Native source: `src/internal/event_loop/thread_pool.c`, `open_job_worker`.

The Unix branch maps `sync` to `O_DSYNC` / `O_SYNC`, but the Windows branch accepts the same `sync` value and opens with `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL | FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS` plus `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` only for directory access. That means `sync=1` / `sync=2` currently has no Windows durability effect.

Expected followup: decide and document the Windows mapping for data-sync/full-sync, for example whether `FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH` is the right approximation and whether `sync=1` and `sync=2` can or should differ on Windows.

### Event bus descriptors should be close-on-exec when process support is enabled

Native sources: `src/internal/event_loop/epoll.c`, `src/internal/event_loop/kqueue.c`.

Linux currently uses `epoll_create1(0)`, and kqueue descriptors also need an explicit close-on-exec setup. Once process spawning is in play, child processes can inherit event-loop descriptors that are unrelated to requested stdio handles.

Expected followup: create event bus descriptors with close-on-exec where the platform supports it, or set `FD_CLOEXEC` immediately after creation.

### Worker shutdown wakeup can be lost if a running worker is freed

Native source: `src/internal/event_loop/thread_pool.c`, worker loop / `moonbitlang_async_free_worker`.

`free_worker` terminates a worker by calling `wake_worker(worker, 0, 0)` and then joining. If this happens while the worker is still inside `job->worker(job)`, the wakeup can arrive before the worker sets `waiting = 1`. After the job returns, the worker sets `waiting = 1`, publishes completion, and then waits, so the earlier termination wakeup can be lost.

This may be unreachable through the intended MoonBit event-loop scheduling path, which normally frees idle workers, but the FFI shape itself does not encode that invariant.

Expected followup: add an explicit terminating state, or otherwise make `free_worker` robust when called while a worker is still running a job.

### Windows directory buffer minimum size counts UTF-16 units as bytes

Native source: `src/fs/dir.c`, `moonbitlang_async_dir_buffer_min_size`.

On Windows the function returns `sizeof(FILE_ID_BOTH_DIR_INFO) + MAX_PATH`, but `MAX_PATH` is a UTF-16 code-unit count while `FILE_ID_BOTH_DIR_INFO::FileNameLength` and `GetFileInformationByHandleEx` buffer sizes are byte counts.

Expected followup: size the minimum buffer in bytes, e.g. account for `MAX_PATH * sizeof(WCHAR)` for the filename portion, and keep the MoonBit-side directory buffer contract in bytes.

### Signal-killed exit status is still lost in the thread-pool fallback

Native source: `src/internal/event_loop/thread_pool.c`, `wait_for_process_job_worker`.

#512 taught the nonblocking process-result path to return `-signal` for a child killed by a Unix signal. The later thread-pool fallback, used when pidfd is unavailable (for example Android or older Linux), still returns `WEXITSTATUS(status)` unconditionally. For a signal-killed child that is not a valid exited status and loses the `-signal` contract.

Expected followup: mirror the process-result path by checking `WIFEXITED` and returning `WEXITSTATUS`, or checking `WIFSIGNALED` and returning `-WTERMSIG`; define the remaining wait-status cases explicitly and add coverage for the fallback path.

## Notes

These are not wasm-specific ABI changes. The intent is to fix or clarify native async semantics first, then keep the wasm host port aligned with the native runtime.

title: Track moving MoonBit-visible allocations out of C stubs for Wasm1
body:
## Background

We want to support Wasm1 later. For Wasm1, MoonBit should allocate guest memory
and pass pointers/buffers to the host. Several native C stubs currently allocate
MoonBit-visible values directly, which makes those APIs hard to reuse for the
Wasm1/WASI allocation model.

## Goal

Move C stubs away from allocating MoonBit-visible `Bytes`, `String`, arrays, or
job external objects. MoonBit should allocate the visible storage, and C should
only initialize or fill caller-provided storage.

## Direct C allocation sites to address

- `src/socket/socket.c`
  - socket address constructors allocate `Addr` bytes
  - `addrinfo_to_addr` allocates `Addr` bytes
  - `if_indextoname` allocates returned OS string/bytes
- `src/fs/stub.c`
  - temporary path helper allocates the returned string
- `src/process/stub.c`
  - Unix current environment helper allocates the result array and entries
- `src/process/windows.c`
  - Windows current environment helper allocates the returned environment block
- `src/internal/os_string/stub.c`
  - Windows C-buffer decode allocates the returned string
- `src/process/test_programs/dump_env/stub.c`
  - dump-env test helper allocates returned environment entries
- `src/tls/openssl.c`
  - OpenSSL peer certificate and channel-binding helpers allocate returned bytes
- `src/tls/schannel.c`
  - Schannel peer certificate and channel-binding helpers allocate returned bytes
- `src/internal/event_loop/thread_pool.c`
  - thread-pool jobs allocate MoonBit external objects from C
  - Windows realpath allocates the returned string from C

## Proposed PR split

1. #409 moves socket address buffers to MoonBit allocation.
2. #413 moves socket interface-name output to MoonBit allocation.
3. #410 moves simple fill-return shims to MoonBit allocation: tmp path, env
   capture, OS-string decode, and dump-env helper.
4. #411 moves TLS returned bytes to MoonBit allocation for OpenSSL and Schannel.
5. #412 moves thread-pool job payload storage to MoonBit allocation, including
   explicit queued/running job ownership and cleanup of abandoned native
   resources.

## Acceptance criteria

- No C stub allocates MoonBit-visible `Bytes`, `String`, arrays, or external
  job objects for the APIs intended to be reused by Wasm1.
- Variable-size outputs use caller-provided buffers, with C returning the actual
  required length and copying only when the buffer fits.
- Fixed-size outputs are allocated by MoonBit and initialized by C.
- Remaining native allocations are either transient, host-owned opaque state, or
  explicitly cleaned up without owning MoonBit-visible storage.

## Out of scope

Native handles, OS/library-owned lists, and opaque host resources can remain
host-owned for native builds. They still need a Wasm1 resource-handle story, but
they are separate from C allocating MoonBit-visible `Bytes`, `String`, or arrays.

title: Architecture and UX improvement suggestions for async stdlib
body:
## Context

This repo is planned to become an async standard library for the MoonBit async runtime. I reviewed the current package structure, public API surface, core scheduler/event loop, IO abstractions, fs/socket/process/http layers, examples, and tests.

Overall, the architecture is strong: structured concurrency is a good center of gravity, cancellation is treated as a first-class concern, and the package split is mostly clean. The biggest opportunities before stdlib stabilization are around resource lifetime invariants, cancellation boundaries, API guardrails, and first-user ergonomics.

## Suggested priorities

### 1. Tighten resource lifetime edges

- [X] `fs.walk` opens a directory and should close it after `opendir_aux`.
  - Pointer: `src/fs/dir.mbt`, inside `walk`, after `let dir = opendir_aux(path, context~)`.
  - fixed in #370 
- [X] `TcpServer::run_forever` accepts a connection before acquiring `max_connections`; cancellation while waiting on the semaphore can leave the accepted connection without an owning handler.
  - Pointer: `src/socket/tcp.mbt`, `TcpServer::run_forever`.
  - Possible fixes: acquire before `accept`, or attach temporary cleanup until the handler task owns the connection.
  - fixed in #371 via performing `acquire` before `accept`

### 2. Harden worker-job cancellation semantics

- [x] Queued thread-pool jobs should be cancellable or removable before they start.
  - Pointer: `src/internal/event_loop/event_loop.mbt`, `perform_job_in_worker` / `wait_for_job`.
  - Current risk: if a task is cancelled after a job is queued but before a worker starts it, side-effecting jobs may still execute.
- [X] The worker cap condition appears to use `>` where `>=` is likely intended.
  - Pointer: `running_workers.length() > max_worker_count`.
  - fixed in #371

### 3. Add public parameter validation

- [X] Guard `max_concurrent > 0` in `@async.all` and `@async.any`.
  - Pointer: `src/async.mbt`.
  - `max_concurrent=0` can hang by constructing a zero-sized semaphore.
  - fixed in #371 by adding size validation for `@async.Semaphore(..)`. All `max_concurrent`-like options flow into semaphore eventually
- [X] Apply the same kind of validation to `max_connections` in socket/http server helpers.
    - same as above, fixed in #371 

### 4. Fix platform cfg typo

- [X] `src/socket/addr.mbt` uses `platfrom` instead of `platform` in the `AddrInfo::free` cfg attributes.
  - This likely affects Windows binding selection.
  - fixed in #371

### 5. Harden HTTP before stdlib stabilization

- [ ] Add maximum request-line/header-line/header-total limits.
  - Pointer: `src/http/parser.mbt`, `Reader::read_headers` and request/response line reads currently use unbounded `read_until("\r\n")`.
- [ ] ~Consider a real `Headers` type instead of `Map[String, String]` with comma-joined duplicates.~
  - ~This preserves duplicate header fields and avoids special-case lossiness.~
  - currently considered won't-fix. See comment below
- [ ] Consider making request/response body limits configurable for servers.

## Architecture notes

- Keep structured concurrency as the primary model. It is the clearest and most valuable part of the design.
- Make runtime-managed exceptions explicit: raw coroutines in `Lazy`, event-loop jobs, and JS promise bridging should each have documented lifecycle/cancellation rules.
- Consider an explicit runtime/configuration surface over time: worker count, signal policy, debug/leak diagnostics, and backend capability reporting.
- Define a small cancellation contract per operation class: not started, submitted but cancellable, submitted and must complete, cleanup shielded. Some of this exists implicitly today; making it explicit would help avoid fs/process surprises.

## User experience notes

- `@io.Reader` exposes `_get_internal_buffer` and `_direct_read` in the public trait. Even if these are for implementers only, users will see them in docs. If MoonBit allows it, split consumer API from implementer API; otherwise document custom reader/writer implementation very clearly.
- `@io.Data` currently serves both write input and read output. The code comment already notes this. Before stdlib stabilization, consider splitting it into separate concepts, e.g. input conversion vs returned body/bytes.
- Add scoped helpers for manual-close APIs, for example `with_get_stream(uri, fn(response, body) { ... })`, so streaming HTTP fits the structured-concurrency/resource-safety model.
- Review examples with “users will copy this” in mind. For example, the file server example should avoid unsafe path concatenation and should escape HTML output.

## Validation observed

From local checkout:

- `moon check --target all`: passed.
- `moon check --target native --warn-list +73`: passed with 45 style warnings, mostly unnecessary package qualifications.
- `moon test --target js`: passed, 225/225.
- `moon test --target native`: 479/488 passed, 9 failed.

The native failures clustered around file-lock/process tests that rely on fixed sleeps/tick buckets. They look timing-sensitive on this machine. These tests would be more robust with explicit handshakes over pipes/queues instead of elapsed-time assumptions.

title: Add UDP socket builder / multicast support for @socket.UdpServer
body:
## Summary

It would be useful for `moonbitlang/async/socket` to support UDP socket configuration before `bind()`, especially for multicast use cases.

A concrete use case is SOME/IP Service Discovery (SOME/IP-SD), which uses UDP multicast, commonly on port `30490`. A receiver typically needs to:

- create a UDP socket
- set `SO_REUSEADDR` before `bind()`
- set `SO_REUSEPORT` before `bind()` on platforms where it is needed, especially macOS/BSD-style systems
- bind to `0.0.0.0:30490` or another listen address
- join a multicast group with `IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP`
- optionally set:
  - `IP_MULTICAST_IF`
  - `IP_MULTICAST_TTL`
  - `IP_MULTICAST_LOOP`

At the moment, `UdpServer::new()` creates the UDP socket and immediately binds it before returning the `UdpServer`. This makes it hard for users to configure socket options that must be set before `bind()`.

## Current behavior

The current `UdpServer::new()` flow appears to be roughly:

```moonbit
let sock = make_udp_socket(family, context~)
...
if bind_ffi(sock, addr) != 0 {
  @os_error.check_errno(context)
}
...
{ io: @event_loop.IoHandle::from_fd(sock, kind=Socket), family }
````

Reference:

[https://mooncakes.io/assets/moonbitlang/async/socket/udp.mbt.html](https://mooncakes.io/assets/moonbitlang/async/socket/udp.mbt.html)

This is great for ordinary UDP unicast, but it does not leave a public extension point for pre-bind socket options.

## Why this matters

Some protocols need UDP multicast or multi-process UDP binding behavior.

Examples:

* SOME/IP-SD service discovery
* mDNS-like discovery protocols
* local-network discovery protocols
* test setups where multiple processes need to bind the same UDP port
* tools that need to listen to multicast announcements from existing applications

For these cases, setting `SO_REUSEADDR` / `SO_REUSEPORT` after `UdpServer::new()` is too late, because the socket has already been bound.

Joining a multicast group after bind may be possible in some cases if users can get the fd, but the lack of pre-bind reuse options still prevents reliable multicast receivers on common platforms.

## Possible API designs

### Option A: add options to `UdpServer::new`

```moonbit
pub fn UdpServer::new(
  addr : Addr,
  dual_stack? : Bool = true,
  reuse_addr? : Bool = false,
  reuse_port? : Bool = false,
) -> UdpServer raise
```

This would be a minimal change and similar in spirit to the existing TCP/HTTP `reuse_addr` support.

### Option B: add a UDP socket builder

```moonbit
let udp = UdpServer::builder(addr)
  .reuse_addr(true)
  .reuse_port(true)
  .multicast_loop_v4(true)
  .multicast_ttl_v4(1)
  .join_multicast_v4(group, iface)
  .bind()
```

This would scale better as more socket options are added.

### Option C: expose `from_fd` / `from_preconfigured_fd`

```moonbit
pub fn UdpServer::from_fd(
  fd : @fd_util.Fd,
  family : AddrFamily,
) -> UdpServer
```

This would allow users to configure special sockets through FFI and then hand the fd to the MoonBit async runtime.

For example, a user could create and configure a socket in C/Rust FFI:

```text
socket()
setsockopt(SO_REUSEADDR)
setsockopt(SO_REUSEPORT)
bind()
setsockopt(IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP)
fcntl(O_NONBLOCK)
```

Then pass the fd into `UdpServer::from_fd(...)` and continue using `recvfrom` / `sendto` in MoonBit async code.

This may be the most flexible option, even if multicast-specific helpers are not added immediately.

## Suggested multicast-specific helpers

For IPv4 multicast, possible APIs could include:

```moonbit
pub fn UdpServer::join_multicast_v4(
  self : UdpServer,
  group : Ipv4Addr,
  iface : Ipv4Addr,
) -> Unit raise

pub fn UdpServer::leave_multicast_v4(
  self : UdpServer,
  group : Ipv4Addr,
  iface : Ipv4Addr,
) -> Unit raise

pub fn UdpServer::set_multicast_if_v4(
  self : UdpServer,
  iface : Ipv4Addr,
) -> Unit raise

pub fn UdpServer::set_multicast_ttl_v4(
  self : UdpServer,
  ttl : Int,
) -> Unit raise

pub fn UdpServer::set_multicast_loop_v4(
  self : UdpServer,
  enabled : Bool,
) -> Unit raise
```

IPv6 equivalents could be added later or included in the same API if desired.

## Expected behavior

A MoonBit program should be able to create a UDP multicast receiver, for example:

```moonbit
let sd = UdpServer::builder(Addr::parse("0.0.0.0:30490"))
  .reuse_addr(true)
  .reuse_port(true)
  .join_multicast_v4(
    group=Ipv4Addr::parse("224.224.224.245"),
    iface=Ipv4Addr::parse("0.0.0.0"),
  )
  .bind()
```

Then use the existing async API:

```moonbit
let buf = FixedArray::make(2048, b'\x00')
let (n, peer) = sd.recvfrom(buf).await
```

## Platform notes

This is mainly needed for the native backend.

The exact semantics of `SO_REUSEADDR` and `SO_REUSEPORT` differ across Linux/macOS/BSD, so the API could document platform-specific behavior.

For multicast, the important part is that reuse options must be configurable before `bind()`.

## Related existing work

There is already merged support for a `reuse_addr` option in TCP/HTTP server code:

[https://github.com/moonbitlang/async/pull/190](https://github.com/moonbitlang/async/pull/190)

This issue is asking for similar pre-bind configurability for UDP sockets, plus multicast support or at least a `from_fd` escape hatch.

## Use case

I am exploring a MoonBit implementation of SOME/IP tooling:

* `someip-probe call`

  * TCP request/response
  * UDP request/response
* `someip-mock serve`

  * TCP server
  * UDP server
  * request handler
  * response sender
* SOME/IP-SD

  * UDP multicast receiver
  * UDP multicast sender
  * service discovery without relying on an external stack

Ordinary TCP/UDP unicast works well with the current socket API, but full SOME/IP-SD requires multicast and pre-bind socket options.

Thanks!

`moon test --target native` hangs indefinitely when testing packages that depend on `moonbitlang/async` (http, tls, socket).

The generated C file for the test binary is ~7MB (due to async + TLS + socket being linked together). The built-in TCC compiler (`~/.moon/bin/internal/tcc`) hangs when compiling this file — it shows 0% CPU usage and never completes.

```
ps aux | grep tcc
```

The same C file compiles in **0.97 seconds** with clang:
```bash
time clang -O0 -g -I~/.moon/include -L~/.moon/lib \
  -DMOONBIT_NATIVE_NO_SYS_HEADER -DMOONBIT_USE_SHARED_RUNTIME -fPIC \
  ...dylibs... \
```

title: handle `Set-Cookie` properly in `@http`
body:
According to the HTTP RFC, if the same header appear multiple times in a single HTTP response, the semantic should be equivalent to concatenating all the values with `,`. However, as noted in the RFC, in practice the `Set-Cookie` header often violates this specification. It is very common to have multiple `Set-Cookie` headers in a single server response. But the syntax of `Set-Cookie` does not allow concatenation with `,`, because the `Expires=` cookie attribute may itself contain comma. Indeed, most browsers does not support parsing comma-concatenated `Set-Cookie` header. So `Set-Cookie` must be handled specially here.

Currently `moonbitlang/async/http` uses `Map` for storing and passing headers. Since a single key can only occur once in a `Map`, this representation cannot handle `Set-Cookie` properly. There are multiple ways to solve this issue:

1. do not use `Map` for headers
    - pros:
        - the resulting API is very simple
        - it also allow users to conveniently pass other header fields multiple times. Although semantically that should be equivalent to concatenating the values with comma, it is allowed and often simpler to just pass the same header multiple times
    - cons:
        - on the receiver side , users need to handle duplicated header field now. We may automatically concat everything except `Set-Cookie`, though
        - on the receiver side, header lookup become more difficult and less efficient
        - users cannot use map syntax to pass headers now
        - this is a huge breaking change
2. handle cookies separately 
    - pros:
        - users can still use map syntax for headers
        - code that does not involve cookies won't get affected
        - cookies probably need special handling anyway. In fact we may wish to automatically handle cookies for `@http.Client` in the future
     - cons:
         - the API will become more complex, as cookies and other headers are now passed differently

title: Windows build fails: multiple issues in thread_pool.c
body:
## Description

Windows native build fails with multiple issues in `thread_pool.c`.

## Issue 1: STARTUPINFOEXW member access error (line 1655)

```
error: 'STARTUPINFOEXW' has no member named 'cb'
 1655 |     startup_info.cb = sizeof(STARTUPINFOEXW);
```

**Fix:** `startup_info.cb` → `startup_info.StartupInfo.cb`

Note: Line 1641 correctly uses `startup_info.StartupInfo.cb`, but line 1655 is missing `.StartupInfo`.

## Issue 2: Undeclared variable `attrs` (lines 1669, 1675, 1682)

```
error: 'attrs' undeclared
 1669 |     free(attrs);
```

**Fix:** `attrs` → `startup_info.lpAttributeList`

The variable `attrs` is used but never declared. It should reference `startup_info.lpAttributeList`.

## Issue 3: Function name typo (line 1674)

```
undefined reference to `UpdateProcThreadAttributeList'
```

**Fix:** `UpdateProcThreadAttributeList` → `UpdateProcThreadAttribute`

The correct Windows API function name is `UpdateProcThreadAttribute` (singular), not `UpdateProcThreadAttributeList`.

## Note: Additional issue for mingw users

`io_windows.c` uses `#pragma comment(lib, "ws2_32.lib")` which only works with MSVC, not mingw.

Workaround: Use `--moonbit-unstable-prebuild` to add `-lws2_32` dynamically for Windows builds. See [moon-release prebuild script](https://github.com/dijdzv/moon-release/blob/main/scripts/prebuild.py) for an example.

## Environment

- GitHub Actions: windows-latest
- Compiler: mingw64 (GCC)
- moonbitlang/async version: 0.16.4

title: Suggestion: move `examples` folder to root for better exposure
body:
In my opinion, I expect to see "examples" (_PLURAL_) in the top-level of a repo instead of having to look through different folders for them.

I think it would be nice to move the `examples` to the root directory of the repo so that it can be more quickly discovered.

Also, adding an `## Examples` section to your README with instructions on how to run each example (`moon run main.mbt` or whatever is more idiomatic for MoonBit) would be great to have.  That way, when people are just browsing around, they might get curious and attempt to download and run the provided examples.  Then when they see how fast it compiles and easy it was to run, they might try some more things and get more interested in the language.
